messages.author: 4940f180b93c96a1
messages.subject: Simple question about tileMethylCounts
parts:
Hello,

I want to understand how the genome is tiled when we choose to summarize methylation information over tiling windows (for instance, tilling over windows of 100bp using tileMethylCounts(myobj, win.size = 100, step.size = 100)).

I am asking because I am using methylKit_0.9.4 on a data set that was analyzed a while ago using a previous version of the package (not sure which one), and after using the exact same commands, I observe an extra window at the end of each chromosome. Any idea on why theses windows show up?? I assume that the tilling is based on the actual chromosome length set by the assembly defined in read function, right? so why would the number of window change if we precise the same assembly?

Thanks,

messages.author: 4940f180b93c96a1
messages.subject: Re: Simple question about tileMethylCounts
parts:
After browsing the questions asked in this group, I found the answer regarding how tileMethylCounts works (Thank you Altuna!)

"For the tiling, we don't need to have the genome size or assembly since the tiling operation will end when there is no more coverage on a chromosome. So you are right, tiling starts when there is coverage on chromosome and ends when there is no more coverage, and the tiles in between will be discarded if there is no coverage on them."

I am still wondering why, in two different runs starting from the exact same input (i.e Bismark methylation reports), I still have different number of tiles, in particular, at the end of each chromosome. Again, the only difference between the two runs are the package version, the rest (commands, data) is the same. Any ideas ??

Thanks!
